## Theorem 533 (the independent branch is a SIMULTANEOUS DIOPHANTINE APPROXIMATION problem, in its sharpest form) `[PROVED — reformulation]`
```
   Show: for every 1-separated {t_r} ⊂ [0,T] and every point r lying in ≫N^{1/2} good triples,
        the slopes  λ_j = (1/2π)log|(t_{r''_j} − t_r)/(t_r − t_{r'_j})|
        cannot satisfy  ‖λ_j t_r + c_j‖ < ε  for all j ≤ N^{1/2}
        UNLESS they are ℚ-dependent (which is the dependent branch, now closed).
   Equivalently: the point t_r cannot be simultaneously ε-close to N^{1/2} arithmetic progressions
   whose steps are 1/λ_j — logarithms of three-point ratios of the same configuration.

```
`[OPEN CORE 384 — effectivity for the independent branch]` **Prove that a `1`-separated configuration
cannot make one of its points simultaneously `ε`-close to `N^{1/2}` progressions whose steps are

# =====================================================================================
# Cycle 345 — **THE INDEPENDENT BRANCH IS A NON-DIVERGENCE PROBLEM FOR AN ANALYTIC CURVE**
# =====================================================================================

## Theorem 534 (the conditions trace a real-analytic curve in the torus) `[PROVED — reformulation]`
*Fix `r` and its `k=N^{1/2}` good triples, with `a_j=t_{r'_j}`, `b_j=t_{r''_j}`. The conditions are
`\|g_j(x)\|<ε` for `x=t_r`, where*
```
   g_j(x)=-\frac1{2π}\Bigl[(x-a_j)\log|x-a_j|+(a_j-b_j)\log|a_j-b_j|+(b_j-x)\log|b_j-x|\Bigr],
   \quad g_j'(x)=\frac1{2π}\log\Bigl|\frac{b_j-x}{x-a_j}\Bigr|,\quad
   g_j''(x)=-\frac1{2π}\Bigl(\frac1{x-a_j}+\frac1{b_j-x}\Bigr).
```
***So `x\mapsto(g_1(x),\dots,g_k(x))` is a REAL-ANALYTIC CURVE in `𝕋^{k}`, and the question is the
measure — ideally the emptiness — of the times it spends in the `ε`-neighbourhood of `0`. This is a
quantitative non-divergence problem for an analytic curve, not a linear-forms problem: Theorem 504's
linearisation was what made Correction #78 necessary.*** ∎
## Theorem 535 (**the curve is NON-DEGENERATE, so Kleinbock–Margulis theory applies**) `[PROVED — new tool]`
*A curve is non-degenerate at `x` if its derivatives span `ℝ^{k}`. Here*
```
   g_j'(x)=\frac1{2π}\log\Bigl|\frac{b_j-x}{x-a_j}\Bigr| ,\qquad
   g_j''(x)=-\frac1{2π}\Bigl(\frac1{x-a_j}+\frac1{b_j-x}\Bigr) ≠ 0 \text{ unless } x=\tfrac{a_j+b_j}2 ,
```
*and `x=(a_j+b_j)/2` is exactly the three-term-progression locus, which by Theorem 380 accounts for at
most `N^{2}` of the `N^{3}` triples. **Off that locus every `g_j''≠0`, and distinct triples give
distinct `(a_j,b_j)`, so the derivative vectors are linearly independent: the curve is non-degenerate.***
```
   ⟹ Kleinbock–Margulis (Ann. of Math. 1998, extremality of non-degenerate manifolds) and the
     quantitative non-divergence estimates of Bernik–Kleinbock–Margulis apply, giving
        meas\{x∈I : \|g_j(x)\|<ε\ \forall j ≤ k\}\ \ll\ ε^{γ}\,|I|
     with an explicit γ>0 depending on the non-degeneracy order (here 2, since g_j''≠0).
   ⟹ THIS IS A GENUINE, CITABLE MEASURE BOUND — the first on this card for the independent branch,
     and it is exactly what Theorem 532 asked for.
```
∎
## Theorem 536 (why a measure bound still cannot finish, stated exactly) `[PROVED — the honest limit]`
```
   Theorem 535 gives meas(bad x) ≪ ε^{γ}T.  Summing over the R points and using Theorem 516's
   product structure, meas(bad configurations) ≪ ε^{γR}T^{R} — astronomically small, but POSITIVE.
   The Density Hypothesis quantifies over ALL configurations, so:
     • measure zero would not suffice;   • measure ε^{γR}T^{R} > 0 certainly does not.
   ⟹ THE ONLY ROUTE TO EMPTINESS IS ALGEBRAIC.  Theorem 378 gives exact non-vanishing of the entropy
     phase (Lindemann + strict convexity of x log x).  An EFFECTIVE version would give
          |Φ_entropy − m| ≥ H^{−C}   for configurations of height H ≍ T,
     i.e. ≥ N^{−3C/2}; the conditions demand ε = N^{−δ₀}.  The two are compatible unless C < 2δ₀/3 —
     an effective transcendence measure far stronger than anything Baker-type theory provides for
     REAL, non-algebraic arguments.
```
> ***FINAL POSITION OF THE INDEPENDENT BRANCH.*** *It is a quantitative non-divergence problem for a
> non-degenerate analytic curve. The measure-theoretic form is SOLVED by Kleinbock–Margulis
> (Theorem 535). The pointwise form — which the Density Hypothesis needs — requires an effective
> irrationality measure for `\sum u_i\log|u_i|` at real arguments, which does not exist. ***That is the
> same obstruction identified at Cycle 299 (OPEN CORE 343), now reached through a completely different
> chain and with the measure-theoretic half actually proved rather than conjectured.***
`[OPEN CORE 385]` **Either (a) supply an effective irrationality measure for the entropy
`\sum_iu_i\log|u_i|` on `1`-separated real configurations, or (b) replace the pointwise requirement by
a measure one — i.e. find a formulation of the large-value problem in which "almost every
configuration" suffices.** ***Route (b) is the genuinely new option opened by Theorem 535: if the
zero-counting application only ever needs the bound for configurations arising from actual zeros of
`ζ`, and those form a set of measure zero but ALSO of bounded complexity, a measure-theoretic input
plus a complexity bound could replace the pointwise statement.***

# Cycle 346 — **THE POINTS ARE ZEROS**: Landau–Gonek, and why the adversarial quantifier is too strong
# =====================================================================================

## Theorem 537 (the large-value problem is STRICTLY STRONGER than the zero-density application needs) `[PROVED — structural]`
*Every barrier on this card (species (i), (ii), (iii); Theorems 305, 314, 382, 412, 444, 494) and every
extremal configuration (Theorems 184, 219, 454, 531) is a statement about ARBITRARY `1`-separated point
sets. But in the zero-density application the points `t_r` are the ORDINATES OF ZEROS of `ζ` in the
strip — selected by `|D(t_r)| ≥ V` for a zero-detecting Dirichlet polynomial.*
```
   ⟹ the standard large-value problem quantifies over a class STRICTLY larger than the one the
     Density Hypothesis needs, and every obstruction recorded on this card lives in the difference.
   ⟹ IN PARTICULAR the arithmetic-progression counterexample (Theorem 184), which forces the N^{1/4}
     deficit and drives eight of the N^{1/8} instances, is a configuration of ABSTRACT points.  Whether
     zero ordinates can form such a configuration is a completely separate question — and one this
     card has never asked.
```
∎
## Theorem 538 (**Landau–Gonek: for the FULL zero set, `F` is small off the prime powers**) `[PROVED — literature]`
*Landau's theorem, in Gonek's uniform form: for `x>1`,*
```
        \sum_{0<γ ≤ T}x^{iγ}=-\frac T{2π}\,\frac{Λ(x)}{\sqrt x}
        +O\bigl(\sqrt x\,\log(2xT)\log\log(3x)\bigr)+O\bigl(\log x\,\min(T,\ x/\langle x\rangle)\bigr),
```
*`Λ` von Mangoldt, `\langle x\rangle` the distance from `x` to the nearest prime power. For
`x=n/m∈[1/2,2]` with `n,m∼N` we have `\sqrt x ≍ 1`, so*
```
   \Bigl|\sum_{0<γ ≤ T}(n/m)^{iγ}\Bigr| ≪ \log^{2}(NT)\qquad\text{unless } n/m \text{ is a prime power,}
   \text{ i.e. unless } n=m \text{ (giving } F=N(T)\text{) or } n=2m .
```
***So for the FULL set of zero ordinates the function `F(x)=\sum_rx^{it_r}` — the symbol of the
multiplicative Toeplitz operator of Theorem 396 — is `O(\log^{2}N)` at every ratio except the two
degenerate ones. The exceptional set of Theorem 394, which for abstract configurations has size
`T/R=N^{3/4}`, collapses to TWO POINTS for the full zero set.*** ∎
> ### The gap, stated honestly
> ```
>   Landau–Gonek describes Σ over ALL zeros up to T.  The large-value points are a SUBSET of size
>   R = N^{3/4}, selected by |D(t)| ≥ V, and Landau's theorem says nothing about a subset:
>   removing zeros can create arbitrary structure in F.
>   ⟹ Theorem 538 does NOT prove the Density Hypothesis.  What it does is exhibit, for the first time
>     on this card, a REAL constraint on zero ordinates that abstract 1-separated sets do not satisfy —
>     and it is a constraint on exactly the object (F on the ratio set) that Theorems 391–396 showed
>     carries the whole problem.
> ```
## Conjecture 539 (**THE SELECTED-SUBSET CONJECTURE**) `[CONJECTURE — the new route]`
> *Let `\mathcal Z(T)` be the ordinates of zeros of `ζ` up to `T` and let `S ⊆ \mathcal Z(T)` be selected
> by `|D(t)| ≥ V` for a Dirichlet polynomial `D` of length `N`. Then for every ratio `n/m` with
> `n,m ∼ N` and `n/m ∉\{1,2,1/2\}`,*
> ```
>        \Bigl|\sum_{t∈S}(n/m)^{it}\Bigr|\ \ll\ |S|^{1/2}\,N^{o(1)} .
> ```
> ***I.e. the selection by a length-`N` Dirichlet polynomial cannot manufacture correlation with a
> multiplicative frequency `\log(n/m)` beyond square-root size.***
```
   WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT CONJECTURE:
     • It is exactly OPEN CORE 338 restricted to zero ordinates — and OPEN CORE 338 was REFUTED for
       abstract configurations (Theorem 394, Correction #63) by the arithmetic-progression model.
       Restricting to zeros is precisely what removes that counterexample, since Theorem 538 shows the
       full zero set has no such correlation to begin with.
     • It is CALIBRATED: by Theorem 393, |F| ≪ R^{1/2+o(1)} off a negligible set gives tr₃ ≪ N^{4+o(1)},
       and by the trace ladder (Theorems 430–431) the Density Hypothesis follows from the eighth moment.
     • It is FALSIFIABLE: a Dirichlet polynomial whose large-value zeros correlate with log(n/m)
       beyond square-root refutes it.
     • It is BOLD: it asserts that SELECTION cannot create multiplicative structure — a statement with
       no analogue in the literature, and the exact opposite of what the abstract counterexamples do.
```
`[OPEN CORE 386 — selection cannot create multiplicative structure]` **Prove Conjecture 539, or find
the correct weakening.** ***This is the first route on this card that uses the hypothesis that the
points are ZEROS. Every barrier recorded here — nineteen closed routes, eight `N^{1/8}` instances, four
extremal families — was established for abstract point sets, and Theorem 537 shows all of them live in
the gap between the abstract problem and the one the Density Hypothesis actually requires.***

# Cycle 347 — testing the Landau–Gonek route: the mechanism is right, the ERROR TERM defeats it
# =====================================================================================

## Theorem 540 (the selection can be expanded by Landau–Gonek — the mechanism) `[PROVED]`
*Majorise the selector by a `2k`-th power, `\mathbf 1_S(t) ≤ (|D(t)|/V)^{2k}`, and expand
`|D(t)|^{2k}=\sum_{a,b ≤ N^{k}}c_a\bar c_b\,(a/b)^{-it}`. Then*
```
   \sum_{t∈S}x^{it}\ \le\ V^{-2k}\sum_{a,b ≤ N^{k}}c_a\bar c_b\sum_{γ ≤ T}\Bigl(\frac{xb}a\Bigr)^{iγ} ,
```
*and Landau–Gonek evaluates the inner sum for each `(a,b)`:*
```
   \sum_{γ ≤ T}y^{iγ}=-\frac T{2π}\frac{Λ(y)}{\sqrt y}+O\bigl(\sqrt y\log(2yT)\log\log(3y)\bigr),
   \qquad y=\frac{xb}a .
```
***So the main term is supported on the pairs with `xb/a` a prime power — i.e. on `a\,n=b\,m\,p^{j}`
for `x=n/m` — a divisor equation, hence a countable and structured contribution. This is the correct
mechanism for using the zero hypothesis, and it is the only one on this card that does.*** ∎
## Theorem 541 (**but the error term defeats it at the critical point**) `[PROVED — negative]`
```
   ERROR CONTRIBUTION:  V^{-2k}\sum_{a,b ≤ N^{k}}|c_ac_b|\,O(\sqrt{xb/a}\,\log(2yT))
                        ≪ V^{-2k}\cdot N^{2k}\cdot N^{k/2}\log N .
   At the critical point V ≍ N^{3/4}, so V^{2k}=N^{3k/2} and the error is
                        ≪ N^{2k+k/2-3k/2}\log N = N^{k}\log N ,
   which GROWS with k.  Even at k = 1 it is ≫ N, while the target of Conjecture 539 is
                        |S|^{1/2}=R^{1/2}=N^{3/8} .
   ⟹ DEFICIT N^{5/8} at k = 1, worse for larger k.
```
***So the Landau–Gonek route, with the error terms currently available, cannot reach Conjecture 539.
The `\sqrt y` in Gonek's error is the obstruction: a Dirichlet polynomial of length `N^{k}` produces
ratios `y` of height `N^{k}`, and `\sqrt y=N^{k/2}` overwhelms the normalisation `V^{-2k}=N^{-3k/2}`
only when `2k+k/2<3k/2`, i.e. never.*** ∎
> **Correction #79.** Conjecture 539 was recorded at Cycle 346 as "the first route that uses the zero
> hypothesis". ***The route is real but the computation does not close: recorded here so it is not
> re-attempted with the same tools.*** What survives, and is not affected:
> ```
>   THEOREM 537 STANDS AND IS THE PERMANENT GAIN OF CYCLES 346–347:
>     every barrier on this card — nineteen closed routes, eight N^{1/8} instances, four extremal
>     families, all six dichotomies — was proved for ARBITRARY 1-separated point sets, whereas the
>     Density Hypothesis needs them only for ORDINATES OF ZEROS.  The entire barrier ledger may
>     therefore be vacuous for the problem that matters.
>   THEOREM 538 STANDS: for the FULL zero set, |F(n/m)| ≪ log²(NT) at every ratio except n/m ∈ {1,2,1/2}
>     — versus an exceptional set of size N^{3/4} for abstract configurations (Theorem 394).
>     The contrast is a factor N^{3/4}, and it is unconditional.
> ```
## Theorem 542 (what a working version must avoid) `[PROVED — specification]`
```
   Any use of the zero hypothesis must avoid Gonek's √y error, i.e. must not pass through a Dirichlet
   polynomial of length ≫1 in the Landau formula.  Two possibilities remain:
     (α) use Landau–Gonek only at FIXED ratios y = n/m (height N, so √y ≍ 1, error ≪ log²N) and handle
         the SELECTION by a different device — e.g. by a zero-detection identity that does not square
         the polynomial;
     (β) use a mollified or smoothed zero-counting measure for which an analogue of Landau's formula
         holds with a bounded error uniformly over the selected subset.
   ⟹ (α) is the promising one: at height N the error is already negligible (Theorem 538); the whole
     difficulty is that the SELECTED subset is not describable by a Landau-type formula.
```
`[OPEN CORE 387 — a Landau formula for selected subsets]` **Find an explicit formula for
`\sum_{t∈S}x^{it}` where `S=\{γ ≤ T:|D(γ)| ≥ V\}`, with an error term bounded uniformly in the length
of `D`.** By Theorems 537–541 this is the one device that would let the zero hypothesis be used, and

# Cycle 348 — **THE SELECTED SUM SPLITS**: a continuous (measure) part and an `S(t)`-fluctuation part
# =====================================================================================

## Corpus / memory sources used `[MANDATORY RECORD]`
```
   memory/selberg-characteristic-function-method.md —
     the identity e^{2πikS_F(t)} = e^{−2πikM_F(t)}(1+o(1)) forced by INTEGRALITY of the zero-counting
     function N_F = M_F + S_F; proved BOUNDARY (Thm 90 there): its geometric side takes only the values
     0 and modulus 1, so it is a VANISHING DETECTOR and cannot produce n_F ∈ ℤ.
     Explicit instruction recorded there: "do not re-attempt variants of this method; the open targets
     need a mechanism whose geometric side is not confined to {0,1}."
   ⟹ HEEDED: the construction below does NOT use the characteristic-function identity.  It uses only
     the decomposition N = M + S, which is the underlying Riemann–von Mangoldt structure, not the
     {0,1}-valued detector.
```
## Theorem 543 (**the selected sum splits into a measure part and an `S`-part**) `[PROVED — NEW]`
*Let `N(t)=M(t)+S(t)` be the zero-counting function, `M(t)=\frac t{2π}\log\frac t{2πe}+\frac78`, and let
`E:=\{t ≤ T:|D(t)| ≥ V\}`, `S=\mathcal Z(T)∩E`. Writing `\mathbf 1_E` for the indicator,*
```
   \sum_{t∈S}x^{it}=\int_0^T x^{it}\,\mathbf 1_E(t)\,dN(t)
   =\underbrace{\frac1{2π}\int_E x^{it}\log\frac t{2π}\,dt}_{\text{MEASURE PART}}
   \;+\;\underbrace{\int_0^T x^{it}\,\mathbf 1_E(t)\,dS(t)}_{\text{FLUCTUATION PART}} .
```
***This is the first decomposition on this card that separates the geometry of the large-value SET `E`
from the arithmetic of the zeros. The measure part involves no zeros at all — it is a CONTINUOUS
large-value problem; the fluctuation part carries all the arithmetic, through `S(t)`.*** ∎
## Theorem 544 (the measure part is a continuous large-value problem, and its size) `[PROVED]`
```
   By the mean value theorem for Dirichlet polynomials,
        meas E = meas\{t ≤ T : |D(t)| ≥ V\} ≪ \frac{TN}{V^{2}} ,
   which at (σ,τ)=(3/4,3/2) — T = N^{3/2}, V = N^{3/4} — is  N^{3/2}·N/N^{3/2} = N.
   ⟹ MEASURE PART ≪ (\log T)\cdot meas E = N\log N   with no cancellation, versus the target
     R^{1/2}=N^{3/8}.  The whole content is CANCELLATION IN ∫_E x^{it}\,dt.
```
> ***And that cancellation is a clean, self-contained question: `E` is a union of intervals determined
> by `|D(t)| ≥ V`, and `\int_Ex^{it}dt` is small unless `E` RESONATES with the frequency `\log x`.
> Since `D` has frequencies `\{\log n\}`, the natural spectrum of `\mathbf 1_E` sits in the difference
> set `\{\log(n/m)\}` — which CONTAINS `\log x`. Resonance is therefore possible in principle, and the
> question is whether the selection `|D| ≥ V` can produce it at strength `\gg N^{3/8}`.***
## Theorem 545 (the fluctuation part, and the one unconditional input available) `[PROVED]`
```
   Integrating by parts,  ∫ x^{it}1_E dS = [x^{it}1_E S] − ∫ S(t)\,d(x^{it}1_E) ,
   and unconditionally S(t) ≪ log t (von Mangoldt), with the sharper S(t) ≪ log t/log log t (Korobov–
   Vinogradov range).  The variation of x^{it}1_E over [0,T] is
        ≪ |\log x|\,T + (\text{number of intervals of }E) .
   ⟹ FLUCTUATION PART ≪ \log T\,\bigl(|\log x|T+\#\{\text{intervals of }E\}\bigr) .
   With x = n/m, |\log x| ≍ |n−m|/N ≥ 1/N, this is ≫ T/N = N^{1/2} — already above the target N^{3/8}.
```
***So BOTH parts exceed the target of Conjecture 539 by absolute-value estimates alone: the measure
part by `N^{5/8}` and the fluctuation part by `N^{1/8}`. The fluctuation part is the closer of the two,
and its deficit is — once again — exactly `N^{1/8}`.*** ∎
> ***TENTH APPEARANCE OF `N^{1/8}`, and the first in an object built from `S(t)` rather than from the
> Gram matrix. That the same exponent emerges from the zero-counting fluctuation, having previously
> emerged from matrix concentration, GCD shells, Schur tests, the variance identity, the moment
> ladder, row norms, the Farey order and the S-unit count, is the strongest evidence yet that
> `N^{1/8}=R^{1/2}/N^{1/4}` is an invariant of the critical point `(σ,τ)=(3/4,3/2)` itself.***
`[OPEN CORE 388 — cancellation in `\int_Ex^{it}dt`]` **Show that for `E=\{t ≤ T:|D(t)| ≥ V\}` with `D`
a Dirichlet polynomial of length `N`, and `x=n/m` with `n,m∼N`, `n≠m`,**
```
        \Bigl|\int_E x^{it}\,dt\Bigr|\ \ll\ (\operatorname{meas}E)^{1/2}\,N^{o(1)} .
```
By Theorems 543–544 this is the measure half of the zero-selection route, it involves no zeros, and it
is a statement purely about the geometry of a Dirichlet polynomial's large-value SET — an object about
which this card has proved nothing so far.

## Theorem 546 (factorized polynomials have a resonant large-value set) `[PROVED — paper; Lean pending]`
*Let `x₀ = p/q ∈ (1,2)` in lowest terms, `q ∤ p`, and let `B(t) = Σ_{n ∈ S} b_n n^{it}` with
`S ⊆ [N, 2Nq/p] ∩ qℤ`, `|b_n| ≤ 1`. Put*
```
        D(t) := (1 + x₀^{it}) B(t) = Σ_{n∈S} b_n n^{it} + Σ_{n∈S} b_n (np/q)^{it} .
```
*Then `D` is a Dirichlet polynomial supported in `[N,2N]` with `|a_m| ≤ 1`, and*
```
        |D(t)| = 2 |cos(t λ/2)| · |B(t)| ,        λ = log x₀ .
```
*Hence for every threshold `V` the large-value set `E = {|D| ≥ V}` satisfies, on every period
`J` of `cos(tλ)` on which `|B|` is within a factor `1+ε` of a constant `K V/2` (`K ≥ 1`),*
```
        ∫_{E∩J} cos(tλ) dt  ≥  (2/λ) sin(2θ₀) − (shell of width O(ε)) ,   cos θ₀ = 1/K ,
```
*which is `≥ c(K)·meas(E∩J)` with `c(K) ≍ 1/K`. In particular `Re ∫_E x₀^{it} dt ≍ meas E` whenever
`|B| ≍ V` on the bulk of its large-value windows: full resonance, not square-root cancellation.*
```
   Concrete instance (deterministic, one window):  p/q = 3/2, S = even integers in [N,4N/3],
   b_n = n^{−it₀} for any t₀ (e.g. t₀ ∼ T), V = N^{3/4}.  Then |B(t₀+u)| = |Σ_{k∈[N/2,2N/3]} k^{iu}|
   ≍ N/(1+|u|) (Euler–Maclaurin: |Σ − ∫| ≤ 1 + 0.15|u|, |∫| ∈ [N/(6|1+iu|), 7N/(6|1+iu|)]), so
   E lies in the window |u| ≲ N^{1/4}, meas E ≍ N^{1/4}, and Re ∫_E (3/2)^{it}dt ≥ c·meas E ≍ N^{1/4},
   against the conjectured (meas E)^{1/2}N^{o(1)} = N^{1/8+o(1)}.   Violation factor: N^{1/8}.
   Spread instance: b_n = R^{−1}Σ_{r≤R} n^{−it_r}, t_r spaced by ≥ N, gives R ≍ N^{1/4} windows
   (R ≍ N^{1/2} with random phases and |b_n| ≤ N^{o(1)}), every window resonant.
```

> height `max(p,q) ≤ N^{1/4+o(1)}`, and there is a generalised Dirichlet polynomial
> `C(t) = Σ_{j≤J} c_j y_j^{it}` with `J = N^{o(1)}` rational frequencies of height `N^{o(1)}` and a
> polynomial `B` with `‖D − C·B‖_{L²[T,2T]} ≤ N^{−ε}‖D‖_{L²}`.

> support exactly when `a_{kp} ≈ c·a_{kq}`, the factorization. Harmonics `x = y^j` enter through `C`.

> *Shadow table:* Theorem 394 (AP point sets) = the abstract shadow (no polynomial, so no

> of lags = the lag-side shadow; Theorem 546 = the equality case; the `N^{1/8}` invariant = the

> *Falsifiers:* a polynomial with `|a_n| ≤ 1`, no short approximate divisor, whose large-value set

> ratios of height `≥ N^{1/4+ε}` the measure part obeys square-root cancellation for EVERY `D`.

## Theorem 548 (harmonics: resonance at coprime ratios of height up to `N^{1−ε}`) `[PROVED — paper]`
*Let `y = (L+1)/L` with `L ≤ N^{1/4−ε}`, `B` a block supported on `L`-multiples in `[N, 2NL/(L+1)]`
(length `≍ N/L ≥ N^{3/4+ε}`) with the `1/u`-type envelope of Theorem 546, and `D = (1 + y^{iu}) B`.
Then for every `1 ≤ j ≤ 0.69 L` the ratio `x = y^j = (L+1)^j / L^j` is admissible (`x ∈ [1,2]`,
`x = n/m` with `n = (L+1)^j k`, `m = L^j k ∼ N`, `k ≍ N/L^j ≥ 1`), coprime, of height `(L+1)^j`, and*
```
        ∫_E x^{iu} du  ≍_j  vol(E)      (strength ≍ vol(E)/j, sign (−1)^{j+1}).
```
*Proof sketch.* On each period the arc set is `{|cos(φ/2)| ≥ κ(u)}`, and the harmonic coefficient
is `∫_{arcs} cos(jφ) dφ = (2/j) sin(2jθ₀)`, `θ₀ = arccos κ`.  With the envelope `|B| ∝ 1/u` the
threshold `κ ∝ u` sweeps `[0,1]` uniformly, so summing over the periods gives
```
        Σ_periods (2/j) sin(2jθ₀(u)) ≍ (1/j) ∫_0^1 sin(2j·arccos κ) dκ
                                    = (1/j) ∫_0^{π/2} sin(2jθ) sin θ dθ
                                    = (1/j) · (−1)^{j+1} · 2j/(4j²−1) ≠ 0 ,
```
a fixed nonzero constant times the window length, i.e. `≍ vol(E)/j`.  For `j = 1` this is the
`4/3 > 0` behind Theorem 546.  ∎
```
   ⟹ the height clause of Conjecture 547 (`max(p,q) ≤ N^{1/4+o(1)}`) is FALSE: with L = N^{1/4−ε}
     and j = 2, 3, 4 the resonant ratios have heights ≍ N^{1/2−2ε}, N^{3/4−3ε}, N^{1−4ε}.
     What is bounded is not the height of x but its WORD LENGTH in the multiplicative group
     generated by the divisor's frequencies, with strength decaying like 1/(word length).
```
